_provenance.note: Missouri citation authorities. Missouri maintains a SINGLE primary citation family — the DSS Manuals SNAP Manual (soon to be folded into a Combined Income Maintenance Policy Manual per IM-23, April 2025), published section-by-section under a legacy 'food-stamps' URL path, cited by chapter.section(.subsection...) e.g. '1105.035.00', '1115.035.25.15', or the deeper '1105.015.10.35.10'. This pack invents the short prefix 'MO IM Manual' (Missouri Income Maintenance Manual) to disambiguate in running text — matching Missouri's own memo-numbering convention ('IM-50', 'IM-71', etc., short for Income Maintenance) and this roster's convention of an invented short prefix per state (IN's 'IN PPM', VA's 'VA SNAP Manual Part', NC's 'FNS', TN's 'TN Rule'/'TDHS Policy'). Statute citations use 'RSMo §', Missouri's own standard citation form for Revised Statutes of Missouri sections.

patterns.note: Missouri DSS Manuals SNAP Manual, cited by chapter.section(.subsection...), e.g. 1105.035.00 (ABAWD Work Requirements), 1115.035.25.15 (Mandatory Utility Standards), 1105.015.10.35.10 (Exceptions to Felony Drug Conviction Disqualification).
Revised Statutes of Missouri, Title XII (Public Health and Welfare), Chapter 208, e.g. 208.247 (food stamp eligibility, felony drug conviction exception).

moimmanual.note: Maximum Allowable Monthly Income Limits and Allotment — plain federal 130% FPL gross / 100% FPL net limits, no BBCE tier; current FFY2026 figures cross-checked against the DSS SNAP Program Changes Flyer (10/2025)

Categorical Eligibility (CE) — extends beyond TANF/SSI/SAB/SP cash recipients to households receiving specific TANF-funded 'special support services' (Child Care assistance, Community Partnerships); no gross/net income or resource test for CE-qualified EUs

Maximum Resources Allowed — $3,000 standard / $4,500 elderly-or-disabled resource limit. NOT independently confirmed from Missouri's own primary text: this specific subsection returned a password wall on every direct-fetch attempt; figure rests on convergent secondary corroboration (Missouri Budget Project) — see PROVENANCE.md Finding 0
Vehicles — 'Exclude the value of all vehicles,' including recreational vehicles, boats, campers, and motor homes; a genuinely broader blanket exclusion than any prior state in this roster

Earned and Standard Income Deductions — 20% earned-income deduction; Standard Deduction by household size, current FFY2026 figures ($209/$209/$209/$223/$261/$299) confirmed via the DSS SNAP Program Changes Flyer

Amount of Medical Deduction — flat $135 Standard Medical Deduction (SMD) for verified expenses $35.01-$170, built from a $170 Medical Expense Standard (MES) less the $35 federal Excess Medical Deduction (EMD) floor

Child Support Exclusion — legally obligated child support paid to non-household members excluded BEFORE the gross 130% FPL test, net income, and expedited-service income; an income-exclusion mechanism, not an ordinary post-gross deduction

Allowable Shelter Costs — rent/mortgage, condo/association fees, property taxes, structure insurance, utilities, natural-disaster repair costs; vendor payments made directly by outside parties are NOT deductible
Mandatory Utility Standards — SUA $495/NHCS $363/LUA $158/telephone $79, dated to IM-50 (September 2024, FFY2025); NOT independently reconfirmed for FFY2026 — see freshness.json

Able Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) Work Requirements — states the PRE-OBBBA 18-54 age range (stale as of IM-71, August 2023); current federal range is 18-64 per OBBBA, confirmed separately implemented in Missouri's FAMIS/MEDES systems though not yet reflected in this manual text

Exceptions to Felony Drug Conviction Disqualification — implements RSMo 208.247: participant-paid voluntary urinalysis (not self-administered), DBH-approved substance-abuse treatment participation/waitlist/completion/not-needed, compliance with court/DBH/probation-parole obligations, no additional controlled-substance conviction within one year, no more than two total qualifying felony convictions ever

Expedited Service Criteria — gross income (minus child support paid) under $150 AND liquid resources under $100, OR combined income/resources less than shelter costs, OR destitute migrant/seasonal farmworker with resources under $100
Processing Time Frames — standard 30-day ceiling for non-expedited initial applications, with two days' mail time for the EBT card built into the deadline

Certification Periods — initial certification assigned up to 12 or 24 months; this specific subsection does not itself state the elderly/disabled 24-month trigger criteria (confirmed only via secondary source — see freshness.json)
Overview of the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) — introductory chapter of Missouri's SNAP manual

rsmo.note: Food stamp eligibility, felony conviction not to make ineligible, when. — Missouri's modified drug-felony ban, opted out of the federal lifetime ban via the option in 21 U.S.C. § 862a(d), effective August 28, 2014 (S.B. 680 merged with S.B. 727). Fetched directly and in full from revisor.mo.gov with NO access barrier — a genuine contrast with Indiana's equivalent statute in this roster, whose primary text required convergent secondary corroboration instead.
